title: Data Engineering Trends: Snowflake, dbt, and Airflow Gains
body_md:
**TL;DR**

- Snowflake and dbt see increased community interest and adoption.
- Airflow remains a critical component for scaling data platforms.
- Data warehousing professionals are navigating shifts toward modern platforms.
- PostgreSQL continues to be a foundational tool for data engineering tasks.

This week, Snowflake, dbt, and Airflow emerged as key rising topics in the data engineering community. Snowflake's release of the 'data-eng-bench'—an agent-based benchmark for repository-level engineering—has sparked interest, alongside ongoing discussions regarding operational comparisons between Snowflake and Databricks. Meanwhile, dbt continues to be a central focus for pipeline development, though users are actively debating the implications of its new pricing models.

Airflow remains a staple for managing complex, high-scale environments, with practitioners highlighting its role alongside Spark and dbt in large-scale data platforms. Concurrently, PostgreSQL is seeing renewed attention as a reliable tool for diverse data engineering tasks, ranging from managing data transfer bottlenecks to supporting real-time grant funding systems.

Beyond specific tools, the community is grappling with the evolution of the data warehousing role. Many professionals are navigating the transition from traditional batch-oriented warehousing to modern data platform development. This shift is accompanied by ongoing career development concerns, as engineers seek to balance project-based learning with the practical demands of organizational data management.
